task.title: Reuse values with custom properties and functions
task.shortdesc: A custom property holds a value that you write once and use in many declarations. You can give it a type, read values from the attributes of your XML, and define your own functions.

info.p: The name of a custom property starts with two hyphens, as in --accent. Names are case sensitive, so --Accent and --accent are two properties. The value can be any text. A custom property is inherited, so define it on the root element or on any element, and every element below it can use it:
Write var() with the name of the property. A second argument, after a comma, is the fallback for when the property has no value on that element. The fallback can use var() too:

CSSMedia replaces var() with the text of the property, so a custom property can hold part of a declaration, such as 20pt 0 for margin. Custom properties can use each other. If they use each other in a circle, none of them has a value, and the fallbacks are used.
A var() that has no value and no fallback makes the declaration invalid when it is computed, and the property takes the value unset. Inherit, reset and roll back values explains it.

step.cmd: Give a custom property a type

info.p: An @property rule registers a custom property. It has these descriptors:

ul.li: syntax is the type of the value, written as a string: "<length>", "<color>", "<number>", "<percentage>" and the other types of CSS. A bar between types, as in "<length> | auto", allows either. A plus sign after a type, as in "<length>+", allows a list. "*" allows any value.
inherits is true or false. With false the elements below do not take the value, and they use the initial value.
initial-value is the value used when no rule sets the property.

info.p: A value that does not match the type is replaced by the initial value. A registered length is computed where you write it: if you write --size: 2em on the chapter, the titles inherit the length in pixels that 2em is for the chapter, whatever the font size of the title is. If you write the same @property rule more than once, the last one is used.

step.cmd: Read the attributes of your XML with attr()

info.p: The function attr() takes the value of an attribute of the element that you style. Without a type it gives a string, which fits content. After the name of the attribute you can write the type of the value, in angle brackets, and CSSMedia reads the attribute as that type. The last argument is the fallback, used when the attribute is missing or cannot be read as the type:
A string without a fallback is empty when the attribute is missing, and a value with a type has no fallback unless you write one. Place an image shows attr() with the type url.

A @function rule defines a function whose name starts with two hyphens. The arguments have a name, and they can have a type and a default value. The descriptor result gives the value that the function returns, and it can use the arguments with var(). After returns you can write the type of the result. Inside the rule you can define custom properties for the steps of a calculation:

A function can take several arguments, separated by commas, and can call other functions. An argument can be the value of a custom property, as in --double(var(--gap)). If an argument does not match its type, the declaration is invalid when it is computed.
